From b2dd797543cfa6580eac8408dd67fa02164d9e56 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Steven Rostedt (Google)" <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date: Wed, 6 Dec 2023 10:02:44 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] ring-buffer: Force absolute timestamp on discard of event

There's a race where if an event is discarded from the ring buffer and an
interrupt were to happen at that time and insert an event, the time stamp
is still used from the discarded event as an offset. This can screw up the
timings.

If the event is going to be discarded, set the "before_stamp" to zero.
When a new event comes in, it compares the "before_stamp" with the
"write_stamp" and if they are not equal, it will insert an absolute
timestamp. This will prevent the timings from getting out of sync due to
the discarded event.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-trace-kernel/20231206100244.5130f9b3@gandalf.local.home

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Masami Hiramatsu <mhiramat@kernel.org>
Cc: Mark Rutland <mark.rutland@arm.com>
Cc: Mathieu Desnoyers <mathieu.desnoyers@efficios.com>
Fixes: 6f6be606e763f ("ring-buffer: Force before_stamp and write_stamp to be different on discard")
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (Google) <rostedt@goodmis.org>

diff --git a/kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c b/kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c
index 43cc47d7faaf..a6da2d765c78 100644
--- a/kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c
+++ b/kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c
@@ -3030,22 +3030,19 @@ rb_try_to_discard(struct ring_buffer_per_cpu *cpu_buffer,
 			local_read(&bpage->write) & ~RB_WRITE_MASK;
 		unsigned long event_length = rb_event_length(event);
 
+		/*
+		 * For the before_stamp to be different than the write_stamp
+		 * to make sure that the next event adds an absolute
+		 * value and does not rely on the saved write stamp, which
+		 * is now going to be bogus.
+		 */
+		rb_time_set(&cpu_buffer->before_stamp, 0);
+
 		/* Something came in, can't discard */
 		if (!rb_time_cmpxchg(&cpu_buffer->write_stamp,
 				       write_stamp, write_stamp - delta))
 			return false;
 
-		/*
-		 * It's possible that the event time delta is zero
-		 * (has the same time stamp as the previous event)
-		 * in which case write_stamp and before_stamp could
-		 * be the same. In such a case, force before_stamp
-		 * to be different than write_stamp. It doesn't
-		 * matter what it is, as long as its different.
-		 */

-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/trace/ring_buffer.c`**
- The patch modifies the `rb_try_to_discard` function to ensure that when an event is discarded, the `before_stamp` is explicitly set to zero. This change is intended to prevent the use of a potentially invalid timestamp from the discarded event.
- The previous logic that checked if the `delta` was zero and conditionally set `before_stamp` to zero has been removed. Instead, the new logic directly sets `before_stamp` to zero unconditionally when an event is discarded.

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification to set `before_stamp` to zero directly addresses a race condition where a new event could be inserted while an event is being discarded. By ensuring `before_stamp` is zero, the subsequent event will compare it with `write_stamp` and, if they are not equal, will insert an absolute timestamp. This change is a refinement of the previous logic that aimed to ensure `before_stamp` and `write_stamp` are different, but it simplifies the condition by removing the check for `delta`. The overall goal is to maintain accurate timing in the ring buffer by preventing reliance on potentially invalid timestamps from discarded events.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (bpage->page == (void *)addr && rb_page_write(bpage) == old_index) {
    ...
    if (!delta)
        rb_time_set(&cpu_buffer->before_stamp, 0);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when an event is discarded, the `before_stamp` can be set to zero only if the `delta` is zero, which means the timestamps of the current and previous events are the same. This can lead to a situation where `before_stamp` and `write_stamp` are equal, causing a new event to incorrectly use the timestamp from the discarded event as an offset, resulting in inaccurate timing.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
rb_time_set(&cpu_buffer->before_stamp, 0);
```
Reason:
This line ensures that `before_stamp` is explicitly set to zero whenever an event is discarded, regardless of the `delta`. This guarantees that `before_stamp` will always differ from `write_stamp`, preventing any new event from relying on a potentially invalid timestamp from the discarded event, thus maintaining accurate timing information.
